kurz: Almost every sauce is one of three things: an [[emulsion|emulsion]] of fat and water, a liquid thickened with starch, or a reduced juice.
bild_im_kopf: Three tools in the box: a whisk (emulsion), paste (starch) and a pot (reduction). If you know which one you are using, you also know what can go wrong.
was_passiert: Emulsions such as mayonnaise, vinaigrette or hollandaise hold fat droplets in water. Starch sauces such as béchamel or a [[gebunden|thickened]] jus get thick because starch granules [[quellen|swell]]. [[reduktion|Reductions]] become concentrated and silky because water evaporates and gelatine remains.
warum_wichtig: Every sauce problem belongs to one of the three groups. Curdled, split, lumpy or thin: the principle shows the fix.
faustregeln: Emulsion: fat slowly, temperature under control, a go-between such as egg yolk or mustard.
Starch: mix it in cold, bring to the boil once.
Reduction: reduce first, season only at the very end.
